table_rows.text: | S457 response max-age semantics | admit/mined | https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9111.html §5.2.2.1; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.txt §5.2.2.1 | agree | Live source says exactly: “The max-age response directive indicates that the response is to be considered stale after its age is greater than the specified number of seconds.” Independent `len(quote.split())=24`; `quote in live_html=True`. Scope excludes lane class names/equivalence. |

| §4.1 normalization as response-directive reorder proof | reject | Same reopened documents, §4.1 Calculating Cache Keys with the Vary Header Field | agree | Exact phrase “reordering field values when order is not significant” is present; context expressly says “The header fields from two requests are defined to match”. Request-key normalization does not prove arbitrary response policy equivalence. |
| §5.2.2.2 as max-age anchor | reject | Same documents, §5.2.2.1 and §5.2.2.2 | agree | Actual headings are max-age at .1 and must-revalidate at .2, not the wave spec's mistaken pairing. |

| S458 field-specific algorithm | admit | https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/ §8.1 steps 2–4, reopened 2026-11-04 | agree | Policy starts empty and is overwritten by every recognized nonempty token in order; the bounded decoder implements that rule. |

| Blanket response-policy reorder equivalence | reject | https://www.w3.org/TR/referrer-policy/ §11.1, direct public GET reopened 2026-11-04 | agree | The latest recognized policy wins; reversed recognized tokens need not preserve effective policy. This cannot justify arbitrary-header equivalence. |

| S459 CrUX Vis docs | admit (A) | GET https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux/vis → 200, 114607 B | **agree** | Exact quote present: "If your origin is not included in the CrUX dataset, there will be no data to display." (17 words, "Does it work for all websites?"); teaching scoped, no overclaim. |

| S461 RFC 9111 slice | admit (A) | GET https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc9111.html → 200, 178573 B | **agree** | Exact quote present: "either the first occurrence should be used or the response should be considered stale" (14 words, §4.2.1 ¶4); ≤25-word located quotes for all three new rows check out; supersedes-S457 scope correctly narrow. |

| RFC 7234 minimum-duplicate attribution | reject proposition | GET https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7234.txt → 200, 90647 B | **agree** | §4.2.1 says "the directive's value is considered invalid"; no first-occurrence/minimum-duplicate rule exists there (grep sweep), so the historical attribution was false and the primary-source correction is grounded. |
